ask: The company's license or registration number, and its class
Any job-size limit the license has
The firm's lead-safe certificate, for work on older homes where the rules require it
General liability insurance; workers' comp where the business has employees
A bond, where the state's form asks for one
pf.license.holder: The business; plus a qualifying person where the state's form names one. Each painter who works on older homes holds a lead-safe certificate, where the rules require it.

An older home is offered only if the firm's lead-safe certificate is on file, where the rules require it; if not, no time is offered and the customer is pointed to the kind of business that can help
pf.license.small_repairs: Small trim or sill repairs stay inside a paint job only where the state's form says they're part of painting; anything more needs that trade's license
pf.license.drywall: Drywall repair goes live on its own license where the state's form asks for one, and each drywall finisher's own where it asks
pf.license.color_shop: A color consult at the shop needs no license: the shop gives its business registration only
pf.license.renewals: License, certificate, insurance and bond dates kept; reminded 30 days out; a lapse pauses new bookings
pf.license.background: Background checks only where the state's form asks

B.price: quoted after the estimate visit, by the room
B.where: at the customer's place; someone home, or a lockbox

B.price: priced from the customer's photos (example: $640); over $500, Sam OKs it
B.before: a signed contract where the state's form needs one, then a 25% deposit

B.where: at the customer's place; nobody needs to be home

B.name: Fence staining

pf.services.capacity: One estimator or color consultant per booking; one crew of 3 per paint job, 2 crews; the shop's one spray booth is saved for custom finish samples
pf.services.skills: Estimates and running a job: crew leads. Older homes: a certified renovator on the job, where the rules require it. Color consults: color consultants. Drywall: a drywall finisher.
pf.services.nobody_home: Outside work days, deck and fence staining: nobody needs to be home; a start and an end photo each day. Inside work: someone home, or a lockbox.
pf.services.online: A color consult can be a video call (counts as at the shop)
pf.services.recent_range: Before an estimate, the AI may show the business's range of recent jobs (example: exterior repaints ran $6,000 to $12,000), labeled as the business's own numbers, never as a quote

before_times: How many stories? (ladders and the crew's size)
The siding or wall type: wood, stucco, fiber cement, vinyl or drywall
The year the home was built (older homes may need lead-safe work, where the rules require it)
after_time: Any peeling, rot or water damage you've seen?
Does a homeowners' group have rules on colors?
Do you own the home or rent? (the owner must OK the work)
Pets or children at home on work days, how to get in, and where the crew can park
secure_page_only: Photos of the walls or the house (optional)
pf.questions.who_may_book: An adult who owns the home, or someone with the owner's written OK. A renter's paint job needs the owner to sign.
shop: Which rooms, or the outside of the house
Photos of the rooms, or a paint chip you like (optional)

stop.words: a fire, smoke or a gas smell
stop.says: Leave the house now, and call 911.

stop.words: someone fainted, can't breathe, or fell from a ladder

steps_then_go_on.words: a child may have swallowed paint chips or dust from an older home
steps_then_go_on.says: Call Poison Help at 1-800-222-1222 and the child's doctor about a lead test. If the child is very sick, call 911.
steps_then_go_on.booking: goes on; the words stay out of every text and aren't passed to the business

steps_then_go_on.words: old paint flaking or chipping in an older home
steps_then_go_on.says: Keep children and pets away from the chips, and don't sweep, sand or scrape them. We'll treat the paint as lead until it's tested.
steps_then_go_on.booking: goes on; lead-safe work becomes the plan

steps_then_go_on.words: paint fumes making someone dizzy or sick
steps_then_go_on.says: Open the windows and get everyone into fresh air. If anyone has trouble breathing, call 911.

steps_then_go_on.words: water coming through a ceiling or a wall
steps_then_go_on.says: Shut off the water at the main valve, and stay away from wet lights and outlets. Call a plumber first if it's still leaking.
steps_then_go_on.booking: goes on; drywall and paint once it's dry

steps_then_go_on.words: oily rags from staining left in a pile or a bag
steps_then_go_on.says: Lay them flat outside to dry, away from the house, or put them in a closed metal can of water. They can catch fire on their own.

pf.safety.business_line: Questions about whether old paint is safe to remove yourself go to the business's own line

pf.first_steps.before_quote: The estimate visit at the home. Outside, the estimator starts without the customer, who is needed only for the last 15 minutes.
after_contract: The cancel window ends before any work starts or paint is bought, where the state's rules give one

Color samples: up to 3 patches; colors and sheens signed on the color sheet before paint is bought
The work plan, texted before the first work day
prep: Keep windows shut and pets inside on work days
Move cars away from the house, and clear the porch and the walls

Put any gate or lockbox code on the secure page
shop_prep: Bring photos of the rooms, taken in daylight

pf.visit.check_in: Estimate visit: the check-in code at the door, when the customer joins for the last 15 minutes. Each work day: that day's code, or a start photo when nobody is home outside. Shop: the code at the desk.
pf.visit.at_the_visit: The estimator measures, checks the old paint and photographs any peeling or rot; the written quote follows within 2 business days, good for 30 days
pf.visit.older_homes: Paint in an older home is treated as lead unless a test shows otherwise, where the rules require it
pf.visit.changes: A written change order, priced and signed by both, before any changed work. Hidden rot found while scraping is priced this way; not signed by the set time, the crew lead calls and the crew paints around it.
pf.visit.outside_checks: A lead dust test by an outside inspector after the work, only where the rules require one
pf.visit.done: A walk-through with the color sheet; each touch-up fixed and ticked off by the customer before the last bill; then DONE on the last work day
pf.visit.color_disputes: A color the customer signed off is a new, priced change
pf.visit.shop_done: DONE after the consult, with the colors saved on the color sheet for the estimate
pf.visit.before_photos: Peeling paint, soft wood, old stains and anything already damaged

pf.money.estimate: The example's $89 estimate visit is credited to the job; billed only if no contract follows. A free estimate is the safe start.
pf.money.no_money_before_contract: On a paint job, nothing is taken before the contract is signed by everyone
pf.money.deposit: Only after signing; the deposit cap comes from the state's form
pf.money.kept_apart: Money paid before the work is kept apart or bonded where the state's rules require it (a switch from the state's form)
pf.money.no_payment_ahead: Never paid ahead of the work done, where the state's rules say so: the last bill comes after the walk-through and touch-ups
pf.money.samples: 3 sample patches free; more at the owner's price, OK'd by the customer first
pf.money.weather: A move for weather never costs the customer
pf.money.big_bills: Bank transfer through the company's own Stripe for bills over the owner's amount (the example: $500); paid once it clears. A check also works: the crew lead texts 'paid check'.
pf.money.tax: Tax on paint and labor follows the state's form
pf.money.shop: The whole-house color plan's $55 is credited to the paint job if the customer hires Lee Painting; the $20 missed-consult fee only after Sam OKs it

never_in_texts: A child's possible lead exposure: the safety steps go to the customer only, never to the business
Contract and change order papers (secure page only, with a copy by email)
pf.messages.minors: Never booked by a minor; a child at home is never the one who lets the crew in

pf.staff.roles: Crew leads (Tyler, Gabe): estimates, quotes and running each job with a crew of 3. Color consultants (Wren, Hugo) at the shop.
pf.staff.licenses: The company holds the license or registration; each painter on an older home holds a lead-safe certificate where the rules require it; drywall finishers hold their own where the state asks. Color consultants need none.
pf.staff.lead_safe: A certified renovator on each job in an older home, where the rules require it: on site for setup and cleanup, and directing the trained crew
pf.staff.sales: An estimator who sells contracts at the home holds any salesperson registration the state's form asks for
pf.staff.who_oks: Sam OKs quotes and change orders over $500; Pat may OK them too, and Sam's answer wins
pf.staff.stand_in: Another crew lead may take an estimate visit; a job keeps its crew lead unless Sam moves it; an older home's stand-in must be a certified renovator

pf.rules.contract: A written contract for a paint job where the state's rules require one, signed by everyone on title and by the business before any money
pf.rules.contract_parts: The parts the state's form lists (license number, dates, price, deposit, cancel notice, any lien notice, insurance)
pf.rules.cancel_window: A cancel window after signing, where the state's rules give one; work and paint purchases wait for it
pf.rules.lead_safe: In an older home, lead-safe methods where the rules require them: plastic on the ground, nearby windows shut, warning signs, no open-flame burning, power sanding only with a shroud and a HEPA vacuum, and the cleanup checked before leaving
pf.rules.pamphlet: The lead pamphlet the rules require, given before work, with the customer's signed receipt kept
pf.rules.change_orders: Written and signed by both before the changed work
pf.rules.papers: With the last payment: any lien release the state's rules provide, the signed color sheet and the leftover-paint list
pf.rules.show: The license number on the listing, the quote, the contract and the receipt, where the state's rules require it
pf.rules.warranty: 3 years outside, 2 years inside, against peeling or blistering (the example's own term)
pf.rules.records: 7 years; lead-safe records as long as the rules require

pf.edges.weather: Outside paint needs dry wood, no rain on fresh coats, and the paint maker's lowest temperature: the forecast is checked the day before each outside work day; only the affected days move, and a move never costs the customer
pf.edges.hidden_rot: A change order before the fix; not signed by the set time: the crew lead calls, and the crew paints around it
pf.edges.colors_not_signed: Not signed by the set day: the crew lead calls; paint is bought only after sign-off, so the dates may move
pf.edges.new_samples: More samples on request; past the free ones, priced and OK'd first
pf.edges.color_dispute: Goes to Sam; a signed-off color is a new, priced change; the last bill waits
pf.edges.lead_test: A lab test of paint chips can show no lead; then the job may run without lead-safe steps, where the rules allow
pf.edges.mold: Mold under peeling paint: the crew stops there, and the customer gets a written note
pf.edges.cancel_after_window: Sam and the customer settle it; Rosie moves no money on its own
pf.edges.nobody_home: Outside work days: start and end photos
pf.edges.over_license_limit: Not offered, and the owner is told why
pf.edges.other: All other edge cases are handled the generic way

notes:
Pilot: started from the contractor (pattern project). A paint job runs the same way: an estimate at the home, a written quote, a signed contract, a deposit, a cancel window, then several work days and one last bill. What the contractor lacks for painting is added: the color samples and the signed color sheet (B8-x03 to B8-x05) and a forecast check before the coats (B8-x08, B8-x09).
Flow B (main path visit|none|bill): Alex's 1952 house at 28 Cedar Ln. The $89 estimate Thu Oct 22 with Tyler; the written quote, $8,600, Fri Oct 23 after Sam's OK (B8-20 words), good until Sun Nov 22; the contract Mon Oct 26 and Tue Oct 27 with the lead pamphlet receipt (B8-62); the $860 deposit (B8-63); the cancel window to Mon Nov 2 (B8-x01, B8-x02).
Then the samples and the color sheet (B8-x03 to B8-x05), the work plan from Mon Nov 9 (B8-37 words), change order 1 for a rotted sill, $240 (B8-x06, B8-x07), a rain day skipped (B8-x08, B8-x09), a lead dust test where the rules require one (B8-50, B8-51 words), the walk-through with 4 touch-ups (B8-39), DONE Tue Nov 17.
The last bill is $7,980: the $8,600 contract plus the $240 change order, less the $860 deposit (B9-05, B9-06). The receipt is $8,840, with the lien release, the color sheet, the leftover-paint list and a 3-year warranty to Nov 17, 2029 (B10-01). Bank transfer or a check also work (B9-26, B9-09).
The estimate: the old flow's estimate was free. The example business charges $89, credited to the job and billed only if no contract follows, so the master's numbers and its visit-fee path stay true; the plug-in says a free estimate is the safe start (pf.money estimate).
No stage bills: a repaint is a deposit, then one last bill after the walk-through and touch-ups, never ahead of the work (pf.money). B9-21's master what-if (Harper J.'s hallway repaint in 3 stages) stays as it is. Rosfield's $2 for the job comes out of the deposit, the first payment through Rosie (B9-18 more).
Flow A is Sam's second company, Lee Color Shop, a paint color showroom (the master's Lee's Barbershop). Main path list|card|counter: a $35 color consult with Wren, a card saved for the $20 missed-consult fee, paid at the shop counter. A8-x01 offers Tyler's estimate at home, which runs in flow B. A video color consult stays on (A4-01).
A color consult needs no state license: S1-63 '1 A license (the shop)' is off, and rename pairs make S1-49, S1-50, S2-05, S2-06, S2-10, S2-11 and S2-22 say registration only and no license for color consultants. S2-28 keeps both branches (splitsKept): painting and drywall license each person where the state asks (a lead-safe certificate), the shop's people need none. The license-problem what-ifs (S2-12 to S2-14) are about Gabe.
Second kind of work: drywall (trade name Lee Drywall), which waits for Tyler's own drywall license where the state's form asks, like the master's electrical.
Painting is never sent now: the sent-now branches of S2-30, B4-81, B4-16, B6-03, B7-55 and B8-58 are off, and S2-30 says painting and the color shop take none.
Plug-in splits (D24): S1-60 a license, S1-62 and S1-65 the $2, S1-29 no agreement, S1-63 no license at the shop, S2-25 people not spaces, S2-32 no classes, S2-30 never sent now, S11-87 and S11-90 booked by name, S11-92 and S11-94 the $2.
Flow A splits: A3-32 a line for the next color consultant, A4-66 a person's time, A4-43 no paper from others and no form (the test board and 'a problem last time' stay), A5-24 no damage hold, A7-59 by name, A7-62 one person, A7-63 a date that can move, A7-67 no minimum, A7-70 a shorter consult, A8-53 nothing left at the shop, A10-34 a rating. Kept whole: A7-61 (only Wren does custom finishes) and A8-02 (a cabinet door may be required).
